clue.text: Secretary reduced pressure, securing year's writing material

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

indicators.note: securing means holding something within, so the shortened word wraps round the next piece
reduced says the word for pressure is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: pressure is push
YR is the standard abbreviation for year; the 's is just the possessive

explanation.surface: An office secretary, under less pressure, gets a year's supply of stationery.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after year is only the possessive, not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Egyptians wrote on sheets made from the pith of a reed, so it is a material for writing on.

clue.text: Father seizing a new card — it sorts everything out

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the word for father wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: Dad grabs a fresh playing card that solves every problem in the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure-all remedy is supposed to fix every ill, which is what the defining phrase describes.

clue.text: Senior politician, one welcoming leading figure with source of impact on others

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the politician-plus-one pair lets the next piece inside

parts.note: PM is the Prime Minister, the senior politician in Britain
a hero is the leading figure of a story
taken as written

explanation.surface: A senior politician welcomes a celebrity who has influence over other people.
explanation.definitionFit: This chemical, given off by an animal, alters the behaviour of others of its species, so it is a source of impact on them.

clue.text: Searches for weapon, ignoring initial dangers

indicators.note: ignoring the initial means leaving out the first letter of the word just found

parts.note: to frisk is to pat someone down looking for a hidden weapon

explanation.surface: Police searching suspects for weapons, but skipping the first one, invite danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazards and perils are both synonyms, plural nouns for things that may go wrong.

clue.text: Exhausted, without strength, I will have sweet

indicators.note: without here has its old sense of outside, so the word for exhausted surrounds what follows

parts.note: spent means tired out
arm stands for strength or power, as in the arm of the law

explanation.surface: Worn out and feeble, I'll treat myself to a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' has its old sense of outside here, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint-flavoured candy can be called this, so it is a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Note employed by Purcell?

parts.note: the composer Purcell would use musical notes, but the letter C also sits at the exact centre of the seven-letter name PURCELL

explanation.surface: Which musical note did the composer Henry Purcell use?
explanation.walkthrough: Purcell, the English baroque composer, suggests music, but the C is literally in the middle of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The note near the centre of a piano keyboard is a musical note, and C is the central letter of the name.

clue.text: Poem penned by male lecturer, for example

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the poem sits inside the next letters

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A poem written by a male lecturer, given as an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar or pattern to follow can be called this, a fair synonym for an example.

clue.text: Father going round church to avoid dog

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the word for father encloses the next pieces

parts.note: dad is father
to shun is to avoid

explanation.surface: Dad takes a detour around the church to dodge a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The sausage dog, a long-bodied German breed, is one kind of dog.

clue.text: European river over in former capital of Italy

indicators.note: in signals that the letter for over goes inside the old currency

parts.note: lire, plural of lira, the currency of Italy before the euro: capital in its money sense
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A river in Europe passes over an old capital city of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'former capital of Italy' suggests Turin or Florence, but capital means money: the lira was Italy's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: France's longest river, flowing through Orléans and Tours, is a river in Europe.

clue.text: Place associated with buns otherwise bringing tea round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for tea encloses the word for otherwise

parts.note: cha (or char) is slang for tea
else means otherwise

explanation.surface: A bakery known for buns, or else one that serves tea all round.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chelsea bun is a rolled, currant-filled sweet bun named after the London district.
explanation.definitionFit: The London district gives its name to the spiral currant bun, so the place is linked with buns.

clue.text: Requirements ascertained after intervention by Democrat recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole thing is read backwards
intervention means coming between, so the letter for Democrat is put inside the word for ascertained

parts.note: seen means found out or ascertained

explanation.surface: Requirements are confirmed once a Democrat steps in, then withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Necessities or wants are synonyms, plural nouns for what must be provided.

clue.text: Describing secretions in core, going critical after completion

indicators.note: after places the word for completion first and the reworked letters following it

parts.note: end means completion

indicators.note: going critical, as a nuclear reactor does, implies the letters break up and reform

explanation.surface: A report on what goes on in a reactor core when it goes critical after the run ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going critical' rearranges IN CORE as OCRINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Glands of this kind secrete hormones straight into the blood, so the adjective describes secretions.

clue.text: Monastic call is to source of religion, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A monastic calling is the route to the origin of faith, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister is the covered walk of a monastery, so the adjective means monastic or secluded.

clue.text: Spots no end of gimcrack device details

indicators.note: no means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: specks are small spots

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Spotting the faults is endless with a gimcrack gadget's specifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of gimcrack' takes the K out of SPECKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for specifications, the technical data listed for a piece of equipment.

clue.text: Obscure alto replacing contralto for an audience

indicators.note: replacing signals that one letter is swapped for another in the word for obscure

parts.note: to cloud something is to obscure it
C is an abbreviation for contralto in vocal scores
A is an abbreviation for alto in vocal scores

explanation.surface: A dull alto has to stand in for the contralto before an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking audibly, so that listeners can hear, is the same as saying it for an audience.

clue.text: Debate inclusion of 'beer' in dictionary? I start to complain

indicators.note: inclusion of means one word is put inside another

parts.note: ale is beer

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: I begin to grumble about the word 'beer' appearing in a dictionary at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of logical discussion and argument, so it is a fair synonym for debate.

clue.text: Popular mixture of fun and zeal is something you could catch

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: a mixture implies the letters are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A well-loved blend of fun and enthusiasm proves contagious.
explanation.definitionFit: Flu is an infectious illness, the sort of thing you might catch from someone.

clue.text: Expert, against one blocking chimney, stated cost

indicators.note: blocking means sitting inside and filling, so these pieces go into the chimney word

parts.note: a flue is a chimney duct
an ace is an expert
V is short for versus, against
a means one

explanation.surface: An expert objects to one thing blocking the chimney and quotes his price.
explanation.definitionFit: The nominal worth printed on a coin or banknote is the stated cost, as opposed to its market value.

clue.text: Overly precise person identifying dunces?

definitions.meaning: a pedant who fusses about tiny faults
read literally, one who picks out nits, slang for fools

explanation.walkthrough: Nit is British slang for a stupid person, so a picker of nits singles out dunces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant who finds fault with tiny details; read literally, a chooser of nits, slang for fools.

clue.text: A client is, when upset, unlikely to yield

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A client who gets upset is unlikely to give way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without stretch or flexibility will not give, so it is unlikely to yield.

clue.text: Popular trip to the sea is turning dull

parts.note: in means popular

indicators.note: turning means the pieces are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a dip is a quick swim in the sea

explanation.surface: The once-favoured seaside outing is becoming tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland and lacking flavour or interest, so it is a synonym for dull.

clue.text: Some information US lawyer used against corporation

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
corporation is a jokey word for a pot belly, and tum is belly

explanation.surface: An American attorney uses some evidence against a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' here is old slang for a paunch, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A single piece of data or a given fact, so a small amount of information.

clue.text: Conductor is French, though involved in a lot of Roman playing

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the French word goes inside the reworked letters
playing suggests the letters are moved about
a lot of a word means most of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: est is French for is

explanation.surface: A conductor is French, though he takes part in much Roman music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of Roman' is ROMA, which 'playing' rearranges as MARO around EST.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminent musician who directs an orchestra is called this, so it fits conductor.

clue.text: Fish stock emptied out and consumed

indicators.note: emptied out leaves only the outer letters of the word

parts.note: ate means consumed

explanation.surface: The fish stock has been emptied and eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ray-like sea creature, so it is a type of fish.

clue.text: Biting account run by papers

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A cutting report published by the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent or caustic, acrid and biting both describe a sharp smell or remark.

clue.text: I have repeatedly to pen name and another name taking time to be creative

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the letters for name go inside
taking here means taking in, so the doubled letters also hold the second name and the time letter
repeatedly means the short form appears twice

parts.note: I've is a short form of I have
N again for a second name

explanation.surface: I keep trying to write down one name and another, taking my time to be creative.
explanation.walkthrough: The doubled I'VE holds both names: the first N after its opening I, and the N with T between the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of new ideas and original, so it is a close synonym for creative.

clue.text: Bone incorporated hints of unusual surgery

indicators.note: hints of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A bone with signs of some unusual surgery done on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The anvil-shaped small bone of the middle ear is one particular bone.

clue.text: Important person, upper-class one? That includes a Baron

indicators.note: includes means the next letters go inside the word for a toff

parts.note: a nob is a toff, an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A grand toff? That sort counts a baron among his set.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally an Indian governor, then a wealthy grandee, so a person of importance.

clue.text: Sensible to avoid first cape when apprehending one of villains at sea

indicators.note: apprehending means seizing and holding, so the shortened word takes in the next letter
avoiding the first one means the earlier of two matching letters is left out

parts.note: practical means sensible
C is the abbreviation for cape on maps
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: It is wise to steer clear of the first headland while catching one of the pirates.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first C of PRACTICAL leaves PRATICAL; I goes in after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates are robbers on the high seas, so the adjective relates to such villains.

clue.text: Russian stage designer leads in ballet and kindred sundry theatrics

indicators.note: the leads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A Russian theatre designer heads up ballet and assorted related shows.
explanation.walkthrough: Léon Bakst designed sets and costumes for Diaghilev's Ballets Russes.
explanation.definitionFit: Léon Bakst was the Russian painter famous for his designs for the Ballets Russes stage.

clue.text: Works out dictator's imprisoning journalist

indicators.note: imprisoning means locking up inside, so the journalist goes within

parts.note: Il Duce was Mussolini's title, so the dictator's is duce's
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Someone figures out that the dictator has jailed a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer by reasoning is to work something out.

clue.text: Ban the writer returning to pub? Try

indicators.note: returning means turning back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: the writer means the setter, me
a bar is a pub
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Should I be barred from going back to the pub? Give it a go.
explanation.definitionFit: An official prohibition on trade, so a kind of ban.
